title: Inline SVG
summary: Describe sharp vector graphics directly in an HTML document.
nestedConcepts: Give informative icons an accessible name

subtopics.title: SVG
subtopics.explanation: SVG elements describe shapes such as circles, rectangles, and paths. A path is a set of drawing instructions for lines and curves. It is like tracing a route on a map. Inline SVG is useful for icons and diagrams that need to scale crisply, but complex artwork may be easier to maintain as a separate file. For example, a small search icon can use a path and inherit its color from the button text. For example, use a viewBox that encloses the entire path to avoid clipping.

subtopics.title: viewBox
subtopics.explanation: `viewBox` defines the coordinate space used by the drawing. It tells the browser how to map the artwork into the displayed SVG box. It is like the grid on a sheet of graph paper. A correct viewBox helps the graphic scale without clipping, so test the artwork at several sizes. For example, a chart may need a title and a nearby text summary of its important values. For example, a button containing an icon needs a name even if the SVG is decorative.

subtopics.title: title
subtopics.explanation: A `<title>` can provide a short name for a meaningful SVG, while a description can explain a complex graphic. This is like adding a caption to a diagram. Make the accessible name useful in the surrounding context. Do not repeat nearby text without adding information. For example, use a viewBox that includes the complete drawing so it does not clip when scaled. For example, a standalone chart needs a text description of its main takeaway.

subtopics.title: Use currentColor for themed icons
subtopics.explanation: `currentColor` lets an SVG shape use the element’s current text color. This makes an icon adapt when a theme changes. It is like using the same ink as the surrounding label. Set a visible color and check hover, focus, and disabled states so the icon remains clear. For example, currentColor lets a monochrome icon follow a button’s hover color. For example, set fill or stroke to currentColor so the icon follows theme text.

subtopics.title: Mark decorative icons as hidden
subtopics.explanation: Decorative icons add no information beyond nearby text. Mark them so assistive technology can skip them, for example with `aria-hidden="true"` when appropriate. This is like leaving a flourish out of a spoken description. For an icon that is the only content in a button, provide an accessible name on the button. For example, an icon next to the word “Search” is usually decorative and should not be announced twice. For example, prefer a real button around an interactive icon rather than adding click to a path.

foundations.overview: SVG is a format for describing scalable vector graphics: shapes are drawn from paths and coordinates instead of fixed pixels. Inline SVG places that description directly in HTML, where CSS can style it. Think of it like a drawing made from instructions that can be enlarged without becoming blocky. Give meaningful graphics accessible names and hide decorative icons from assistive technology.
foundations.whyItMatters: SVG supports crisp graphics and flexible styling, but it needs deliberate names and text alternatives when its visual content matters.
foundations.realWorldUsage: A vector drawing is a recipe for shapes, not a photograph of pixels.
commonUseCases: Show a simple interface icon that follows the theme color.
Render a small diagram that stays sharp at different zoom levels.
Provide a text equivalent for a meaningful chart.

commonMisconceptions.myth: SVG becomes blurry when enlarged like a small bitmap.
commonMisconceptions.reality: Vector shapes scale crisply, though embedded raster images can still be pixelated.

commonMisconceptions.myth: Every icon needs a spoken name.
commonMisconceptions.reality: Decorative icons should be hidden from assistive technology; meaningful standalone icons need a name.

commonMisconceptions.myth: A title element alone explains a complex chart.
commonMisconceptions.reality: Complex information also needs a suitable text description or data representation.

keyTakeaways: SVG elements describe shapes such as circles, rectangles, and paths.
`viewBox` defines the coordinate space used by the drawing.
A `<title>` can provide a short name for a meaningful SVG, while a description can explain a complex graphic.
`currentColor` lets an SVG shape use the element’s current text color.
Decorative icons add no information beyond nearby text.

codeLab.title: Create a Labeled SVG Icon
codeLab.instructions: Add a viewBox and draw a simple check mark. Give this meaningful graphic an accessible name.

sandbox.code:
<svg viewBox="0 0 40 40" role="img">
  <!-- TODO: add a title and check mark path -->
</svg>

codeLab.expectedOutput: The preview or source shows the requested semantic, visual, or interactive behavior.

solution.code:
<svg viewBox="0 0 40 40" role="img" aria-labelledby="check-title">
  <title id="check-title">Complete</title>
  <path d="M7 21l8 8L33 10" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" />
</svg>
